prompt: An NSG has an allow for port 22 at priority 300 and a deny for port 22 at priority 200. What happens to an SSH connection?

choices.text: Denied, at 200
choices.why: Right. 200 is read before 300, and reading stops there.

choices.text: Allowed, since an allow anywhere in the list wins
choices.why: An NSG is a queue, not a sum. The first match decides.

choices.text: Allowed, since 300 is the higher priority
choices.why: The lower number is the higher priority.

choices.text: Refused by Azure, since two rules may not share a port
choices.why: Two rules may share a port; they may not share a priority and direction.

prompt: What is the highest number a rule you write may use as its priority?
hint: The defaults sit far above it.

prompt: Which default rule lets a compromised web server open a connection to the database on any port?
hint: Both machines are in the same network.

choices.text: `AllowInternetOutBound`
choices.why: That lets machines reach the internet, not each other.

choices.text: `AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound`
choices.why: That one admits only Azure's health probes.

choices.text: `DenyAllInBound`, which only covers the internet
choices.why: It covers everything, but 65000 is read before 65500.

choices.text: `AllowVnetInBound`
choices.why: Right. Anything in the network may reach anything in it, at 65000.

prompt: A machine has an NSG on its subnet and another on its network interface. An inbound packet is allowed by the subnet's and denied by the interface's. What happens?

choices.text: It passes, since the subnet's NSG is read first
choices.why: Being read first does not make it final: the interface's is read next.

choices.text: It never reaches the machine
choices.why: Right. Both must allow; a deny in either stops it.

choices.text: Azure refuses to attach two NSGs to one machine
choices.why: It allows it, and Microsoft advises against it.

choices.text: The rule with the lower priority of the two decides
choices.why: Priorities are compared inside one NSG, not across two.

prompt: An NSG allows outbound 443. Why does it need no inbound rule for the replies?

choices.text: Replies come from the `AzureLoadBalancer` tag
choices.why: Replies come from the server that was called.

choices.text: Port 443 is always open inbound
choices.why: No port is open inbound by default.

choices.text: It is stateful: it keeps a record of the flow
choices.why: Right. A rule decides who may start a conversation.

choices.text: `AllowInternetOutBound` covers both directions
choices.why: Each rule has one direction.

prompt: To shut a contractor out, ana deletes the rule that allowed their SSH. They are still connected an hour later. Why?
hint: Which connections does a rule govern?

choices.text: SSH is exempt from NSG rules
choices.why: No protocol is exempt.

choices.text: Deleting a rule takes an hour to propagate
choices.why: The delay is not the explanation; open flows are kept.

choices.text: `AllowVnetInBound` let them back in
choices.why: Nothing let them in again: they never left.

choices.text: Rules govern new connections, and theirs was already open
choices.why: Right. The next attempt is refused; the open session lasts until it ends.

prompt: What is an application security group?
hint: It is set on something you build.

choices.text: A list of Microsoft's addresses, kept up to date
choices.why: That is a service tag.

choices.text: A second NSG that a subnet inherits
choices.why: An ASG holds no rules of its own.

choices.text: A label on network interfaces, usable in a rule
choices.why: Right. The rule follows the role, whatever the addresses.

choices.text: A group of users allowed to change NSGs
choices.why: It groups interfaces, not people; people are lesson 9.

prompt: Why does the shop write its web-to-application rule with ASGs instead of the two web servers' addresses?

choices.text: The rule stays true as servers come and go
choices.why: Right. Membership is set on each interface, not in the rule.

choices.text: Because ASG rules are evaluated before address rules
choices.why: Only priority decides the order.

choices.text: Because NSG rules do not accept single addresses
choices.why: They accept addresses and ranges.

choices.text: Because ASGs make the rule apply across networks
choices.why: An ASG is confined to one virtual network.

prompt: Why are the shop's priorities 100, 3900 and 4000, and not 100, 101 and 102?
hint: Think of a rule needed in an emergency.

choices.text: Azure requires gaps of at least a hundred
choices.why: No gap is required.

choices.text: Room is left for rules added later
choices.why: Right. 150 or 3950 are free for the day they are needed.

choices.text: Rules close together are merged by Azure
choices.why: Rules are never merged.

choices.text: Higher numbers are cheaper
choices.why: Priorities cost nothing.

prompt: The service tag `___` stands for `168.63.129.16`, where Azure's health probes come from.
hint: Its name says which service sends them.

choices.text: Azure's IP flow verify, run locally
choices.why: IP flow verify needs a machine in Azure.

choices.text: A client that asks Network Watcher for verdicts
choices.why: It sends nothing anywhere.

choices.text: The course's model of the documented rules
choices.why: Right. A model reading a compiled template, not an answer from Azure.

choices.text: Microsoft's reference implementation of NSGs
choices.why: Microsoft publishes no such program.

prompt: In the draft, SSH from the web server to the application was allowed. By what?
hint: Look at the number on the matching line.

choices.text: By the default `AllowVnetInBound`, at 65000
choices.why: Right. A rule nobody in the shop wrote.

choices.text: By nothing: the model has a bug
choices.why: The model did what Azure documents.

choices.text: By `AllowWebToApp`, since the source was a web server
choices.why: That rule names port 8080 only; it printed a dash.

choices.text: By `AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound`
choices.why: The source was a web server, not the probe address.

prompt: The shop adds a deny on `VirtualNetwork` at 4000 and forgets the rule at 3900. What does the documentation say happens to a load balancer in front of the application?

choices.text: Nothing, since probes are exempt from NSGs
choices.why: They are allowed by a default rule, which the deny is read before.

choices.text: Its probes are denied, so it marks every machine unhealthy
choices.why: Right. `VirtualNetwork` includes the host's address, so 65001 never gets a turn.

choices.text: Only probes from the internet are blocked
choices.why: Probes come from `168.63.129.16`, not the internet.

choices.text: The load balancer moves to another subnet
choices.why: Nothing moves; the probes just fail.

prompt: A web server cannot reach a new application server on 8080, though `AllowWebToApp` exists. The model says *Deny* at 4000. What is the first thing to check?
hint: Which side of the rule names a group?

choices.text: Whether the NSG has more than three rules
choices.why: The count is irrelevant to this packet.

choices.text: Whether port 8080 is above the default rules
choices.why: Ports have no position; rules do.

choices.text: Whether the deny at 4000 should be at 50
choices.why: That would deny the web tier too.

choices.text: Whether the new server's interface is in `asg-shop-app`
choices.why: Right. The rule was right; the membership was missing.

prompt: A request from `10.20.1.4` to `10.20.2.4` on port 22 meets `nsg-shop-app`. Put the rules in the order the model reads them.
trap: Reading stops at 4000, which matches, so the defaults are never reached.

prompt: Which of these does the default rule set allow? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A machine reaching another in its network on any port
choices.why: Right. `AllowVnetInBound` and `AllowVnetOutBound`.

choices.text: The internet opening a connection to a machine
choices.why: `DenyAllInBound` refuses it.

choices.text: A machine sending data out to any internet address
choices.why: Right. `AllowInternetOutBound`.

choices.text: Azure's health probe reaching a machine
choices.why: Right. `AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound`.

choices.text: A machine in a peered network being refused
choices.why: `VirtualNetwork` includes peered networks, so it is allowed.

prompt: A rule allows `Internet` to `asg-shop-app` on 443 at priority 100. Which packet does it NOT let in?

choices.text: A customer in Recife reaching `10.20.2.4` on 443
choices.why: That one matches source, group and port.

choices.text: An Azure public address reaching `10.20.2.4` on 443
choices.why: `Internet` includes Azure's public addresses.

choices.text: A customer reaching `10.20.2.5`, outside the group, on 443
choices.why: Right. The rule only applies to interfaces in the ASG.

choices.text: A second customer reaching `10.20.2.4` on 443
choices.why: Any number of customers match.
